title: termal_name_source_root given an unrecognised parameter (for example 'root' instead of 'path') silently acts as a clear instead of refusing the call
outcome: A naming request with an unknown or misspelled parameter is refused with a message naming the parameter before side effects. Valid work/path naming and documented work-only clearing retain their existing behavior.
acceptance: Preserved fail-first evidence on the unchanged product shows a termal_name_source_root MCP request carrying an unknown field (for example 'root' in place of 'path') forwarded to the host as an implicit clear. The holder's note distinguishes the incident report, the source diagnosis and the executed witness.

An MCP naming request that carries any field other than the documented ones is refused before any side effect, with a message naming the offending field. The claim's named root, its generation, any pending intent and its evidence basis are unchanged. The HTTP route's existing refusal of unknown fields is kept and covered by a control.

Valid calls behave as before: work with path names the root, and work without path clears it, as documented. Authority, worktree validation, the next-turn and sealed-revision timing, publication and budget behaviour are unchanged. The tool's description states that unknown fields are refused.

The full five-stage gate passes on the exact frozen input, reviewed by independent read-only Codex and Claude children with no outstanding in-scope Medium or higher. Holder notes cite the run directory, the fingerprint and the host verification.
